doc.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019

title: Fort Lauderdale's first mixed band and Cannonball on the street dance
summary: Longo's father hired Cannonball for a street dance, the first mixed band in town; Cannonball's playing melted the crowd and led to the Harold Ferguson Band.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah. And so I hired him for the gig, and as soon as he walked on the bandstand, the street was all filled. It was a street dance. There was a big hush that came over the audience you know. But as soon as he started playing “The Stars Fell on Alabama” it melted everybody’s heart and everybody started dancing. And so then my dad started using him on all the club dates. And then Cannonball got me a gig on an R&B band, what do you call it, we used to play the Chitlin Circuit, up and down the coast of Florida. It wasn’t his band, I was just a sideman, he was too. It was the Harold Ferguson Band.
So this was before he, obviously before he left there and went to New York.
Matter of fact he was having trouble because the Dillard High School was getting on his case for playing gigs like that. But he played like he played. He played like he did when he came to New York.
I just love his playing. And when you said he played “Stars Fell on Alabama,” he recorded that later on of course with Coltrane.
Yes. He played it that night and it melted everybody’s heart, and everybody was dancing and the full moon was out. It was gorgeous.
